title: O Thou Who Wouldst Not Have
description: O Thou Who Wouldst Not Have in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 338.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou who wouldst not have One wret-ched sin-ner die, Who diedst Thy-self my soul to_ save From end-less mis-e-ry, Teach me my course to run, While yet I so-journ here, That when Thou com-est on Thy throne I may with joy ap-pear.

lines: O Thou who wouldst not have
Who diedst Thyself my soul to save
Teach me my course to run,
That when Thou comest on Thy throne
So shall I pass my life’s short day
So shall I love my God
And praise Thee in Thy bright abode

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
